title: Algebra Without the Numbers
question: What changed when algebra stopped being only about solving for x?
hook: Mathematicians found that very different problems shared one hidden shape: a set and a rule for combining its elements.
idea: Abstract algebra studies structures made of sets and operations, a view that unified scattered results from number theory, geometry and equation solving.

beats.prompt: Put these steps in the story of algebra in order.
items: Babylonians solve quadratic word problems (about 1700 BC)
Al-Khwarizmi originates the word algebra (830 AD)
Viete's New Algebra brings fully symbolic algebra (1591)
Peacock's Treatise puts algebra on a strictly symbolic basis (1830)
beats.explain: Algebra moved from word problems to symbols, and only in 1830 was a strictly symbolic basis attempted.

beats.prompt: In the 1800s, mathematicians had separate piles of results from number theory, geometry and solving equations. What happened to those piles over time?

choices.label: They gained a common theme and were unified under shared concepts
They were dropped as the problems proved unrelated
choices.feedback: It is tempting to think unrelated fields stay separate, but these results turned out to share a common core.

choices.label: One textbook merged them all at once, with no history
choices.feedback: Unification came gradually and was only finished in the early decades of the 20th century.

beats.explain: Disparate facts acquired a common theme, and were unified on a common set of concepts in the early decades of the 20th century.

beats.prompt: Match each source of group ideas to what it led to.
pairs: Lagrange's study of the quintic equation
The Galois group of a polynomial
Gauss's study of Fermat's little theorem
Symmetry groups such as the Euclidean group
beats.explain: Several areas of mathematics each led to groups in their own way.

beats.prompt: One step in this account is wrong; which?
steps: Abstract algebra studies sets with operations, called algebraic structures.
Groups, rings and fields are examples of such structures.
The formal definitions came first, and the concrete examples from number theory and geometry were found afterwards.
The scattered results were unified in the early decades of the 20th century.
beats.explain: Historically it was almost the opposite: concrete problems came first, and formal definitions came after the unification.
